title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved ends / King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
part: Night 137 · The Lover and the Beloved ends / King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 649–658 (Night 137, continuing directly from nights-136), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 137 brings the story of Tāj al-Mulūk and the Lady Dunyā, which the vizier Dandān has been telling the army besieging Constantinople, to its end, and returns to the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. After four years before the walls, King Ḍawʾ al-Makān takes the army home to Baghdad, where he finds his son Kān Mā Kān seven years old. He honours the bath-house stoker who once saved his life; the stoker, offered anything he likes, asks only to be chief of the stokers, then of the dung-sweepers, and is finally made viceroy of Damascus under the name al-Zabalkān. Dandān brings back Sharrukān's little daughter Qaḍā Fakān, who grows up with her cousin. Ḍawʾ al-Makān makes his son sultan under the Great Chamberlain's guardianship, falls ill and dies after four years; the Chamberlain takes the throne, the boy and his mother are pushed aside, and she goes to beg help of Nuzhat al-Zamān as the night breaks off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّابِعَةُ وَالثَّلٰثُونَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sābiʿatu wa-al-thalāthūna baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the seventh and the thirty after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and thirty-seventh night,
sentences.n: The small alif over the lām of thalāthūn is the print's own: it spells the word without its long alif (والثلٰثون).

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ شَاهْ سُلَيْمَانَ لَمَّا أَقْبَلَ عَلَى مَدِينَتِهِ زُيِّنَتْ لَهُ وَلِوَلَدِهِ الْمَدِينَةُ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna shāh sulaymāna lammā aqbala ʿalā madīnatihi zuyyinat lahu wa-li-waladihi al-madīnatu
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that Shāh Sulaymān, when he came-towards his city, the city was adorned for him and for his son.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when Sulaymān Shāh drew near his city, the city was decked out for him and for his son.
sentences.n: The night picks up where the last one stopped, with the decorated city. The king's name is again printed in the order Shāh Sulaymān. aqbala ʿalā, “to approach, come towards”. zuyyinat, passive of form II zayyana, “to decorate”; the print marks the doubled yāʾ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلُوا الْمَدِينَةَ وَجَلَسَ الْمَلِكُ عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ مَمْلَكَتِهِ وَوَلَدُهُ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ بِجَانِبِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhalū al-madīnata wa-jalasa al-maliku ʿalā kursiyyi mamlakatihi wa-waladuhu tāju al-mulūki bi-jānibihi
sentences.l: Then they entered the city, and the king sat on the chair of his kingdom, and his son Tāj al-Mulūk at his side.
sentences.i: Then they entered the city, and the king took his seat on the throne of his kingdom, with his son Tāj al-Mulūk beside him.
sentences.n: kursī mamlakatihi, “the chair of his kingdom”, is the regular phrase for the throne. bi-jānibihi, “at his side”: bi- gives the place.

sentences.t: فَأَعْطَى وَوَهَبَ وَأَطْلَقَ مَنْ كَانَ مَسْجُونًا عِنْدَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿṭā wa-wahaba wa-aṭlaqa man kāna masjūnan ʿindahu
sentences.l: And he gave and bestowed, and released whoever was imprisoned with him.
sentences.i: He gave gifts and largesse, and set free everyone who lay in his prisons.
sentences.n: Giving and freeing prisoners are the customary acts of a king's rejoicing. ʿindahu, “with him”: in his keeping.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ عَمِلَ لِوَلَدِهِ عُرْسًا ثَانِيًا وَاسْتَمَرَّتْ بِهِ الْمَغَانِي وَالْمَلَاهِي شَهْرًا كَامِلًا
sentences.tr: thumma ʿamila li-waladihi ʿursan thāniyan wa-istamarrat bihi al-maghānī wa-al-malāhī shahran kāmilan
sentences.l: Then he made for his son a second wedding, and the singings and the amusements continued with it a whole month.
sentences.i: Then he held a second wedding for his son, and the singing and merrymaking went on for a whole month.
sentences.n: The first wedding was held in Shahramān's city; this one is at home. maghānī, “songs, singing” (also “places of song”), and malāhī, “amusements, entertainments, instruments of play”, a stock pair. istamarrat bihi, “went on with it”: bi- here is “in, during (the wedding)”. The print marks the doubled rāʾ.

sentences.t: وَالْمَوَاشِطُ تُجَلِّى لِلسَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا وَهِيَ لَا تَمَلُّ مِنَ الْجَلَاءِ وَهُنَّ لَا يَمْلَلْنَ مِنَ النَّظَرِ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-al-mawāshiṭu tujallī li-al-sayyidati dunyā wa-hiya lā tamallu mina al-jalāʾi wa-hunna lā yamlalna mina al-naẓari ilayhā
sentences.l: And the tirewomen were displaying the Lady Dunyā, and she did not tire of the displaying, and they did not tire of the looking at her.
sentences.i: And the tirewomen paraded the Lady Dunyā in her bridal dresses; she never tired of being shown, nor they of gazing at her.
sentences.n: mawāshiṭ, plural of māshiṭa, “comber, tirewoman”, the women who dress and adorn a bride. jallā, “to display (the bride)”, and jalāʾ, the unveiling of the bride before the company in one gown after another. tujallī li-al-sayyida: the object is marked with li-, as often in the spoken language, and the verb is printed with final ى for ي. The print marks the doubled lām of tamallu and the doubled nūn of hunna.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ عَلَى زَوْجَتِهِ بَعْدَ أَنِ اجْتَمَعَ مَعَ أَبِيهِ وَأُمِّهِ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhala tāju al-mulūki ʿalā zawjatihi baʿda ani ijtamaʿa maʿa abīhi wa-ummihi
sentences.l: Then Tāj al-Mulūk went in to his wife, after he had met with his father and his mother.
sentences.i: Then Tāj al-Mulūk went in to his wife, after he had been together with his father and mother.
sentences.n: dakhala ʿalā, “to go in to” a person, here his bride. The print marks the doubled mīm of ummihi.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالُوا فِى أَلَذِّ عَيْشٍ وَأَهْنَاهُ حَتَّى أَتَاهُمْ هَادِمُ اللَّذَّاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zālū fī aladhdhi ʿayshin wa-ahnāhu ḥattā atāhum hādimu al-ladhdhāti
sentences.l: And they did not cease in the most-delightful of living and the most-wholesome of it, until there came to them the Destroyer of Delights.
sentences.i: And they lived on in the sweetest and happiest of lives, until there came to them the Destroyer of Delights.
sentences.n: The closing formula of a tale: hādim al-ladhdhāt, “the destroyer of delights”, is death. The print sets the elative aladhdh, “most delightful”, as الذّ, as if it had the article, and marks its doubled dhāl. ahnāhu, “the most wholesome of it”, stands for ahnaʾihi, the hamza dropped as in speech. So ends the vizier Dandān's tale of Tāj al-Mulūk and the Lady Dunyā.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ قَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ لِلْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ إِنَّ مِثْلَكَ مَنْ يَشْرَحُ الْقَلْبَ الْحَزِينَ وَيُنَادِمُ الْمُلُوكَ وَيَسْلُكُ فِي تَدْبِيرِهِمْ أَحْسَنَ السُّلُوكِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni li-al-wazīri dandāna inna mithlaka man yashraḥu al-qalba al-ḥazīna wa-yunādimu al-mulūka wa-yasluku fī tadbīrihim aḥsana al-sulūki
sentences.l: And at that, Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to the vizier Dandān: Truly the like of you is one who opens the heart, the sad one, and keeps-company-with the kings, and goes in the managing of them the best of going.
sentences.i: At that Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to the vizier Dandān, “It is men like you who gladden a sorrowful heart, who are fit companions for kings, and who guide their affairs in the best of ways.”
sentences.n: Here the frame story resumes: Dandān has been telling the tale to the king and the army besieging Constantinople. sharaḥa al-qalb, “to open, expand the heart”, to cheer it. nādama, “to be a boon-companion to”, to drink and talk with. The rhyme falls on al-mulūk … al-sulūk: salaka … aḥsana al-sulūk, “to take the best course”.

sentences.t: هٰذَا كُلُّهُ وَهُمْ مُحَاصِرُونَ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ حَتَّى مَضَى عَلَيْهِمْ أَرْبَعُ سِنِينَ
sentences.tr: hādhā kulluhu wa-hum muḥāṣirūna al-qusṭanṭīniyyata ḥattā maḍā ʿalayhim arbaʿu sinīna
sentences.l: All this, and they (were) besieging Constantinople, until there passed over them four years.
sentences.i: All this while they were laying siege to Constantinople, until four years had gone by for them.
sentences.n: hādhā kulluhu wa-hum …, “all this, while they …”: the storyteller reminds us where the listeners are. muḥāṣirūna takes al-qusṭanṭīniyya as a direct object, as a verb would.

sentences.t: فَاشْتَاقُوا إِلَى أَوْطَانِهِمْ وَضَجِرَتِ الْعَسَاكِرُ وَمَلُّوا مِنَ السَّهَرِ وَالْحِصَارِ وَإِدَامَةِ الْحَرْبِ فِى اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-ishtāqū ilā awṭānihim wa-ḍajirati al-ʿasākiru wa-mallū mina al-sahari wa-al-ḥiṣāri wa-idāmati al-ḥarbi fī al-layli wa-al-nahāri
sentences.l: And they longed for their homelands, and the troops grew-weary, and they tired of the wakefulness and the siege and the keeping-up of the war in the night and the day.
sentences.i: They longed for their homes; the troops grew restless, and were sick of the sleepless watches, the siege, and the war that never stopped by night or day.
sentences.n: ishtāqa ilā, “to long for”: ilā gives what is longed for. awṭān, plural of waṭan, “home, native land”. The rhyme falls on al-ḥiṣār … al-nahār.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ بِإِحْضَارِ بَهْرَامَ وَرُسْتُمَ وَتُرْكَاشَ
sentences.tr: fa-amara al-maliku ḍawʾu al-makāni bi-iḥḍāri bahrāma wa-rustuma wa-turkāsha
sentences.l: And King Ḍawʾ al-Makān commanded the bringing of Bahrām and Rustam and Turkāsh.
sentences.i: So King Ḍawʾ al-Makān sent for Bahrām, Rustam and Turkāsh.
sentences.n: amara bi-, “to command”: the verb takes what is ordered with bi-. Bahrām leads the Daylam, Rustam the Persians, Turkāsh the Arabs.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوا قَالَ لَهُمُ اعْلَمُوا أَنَّنَا أَقَمْنَا هٰذِهِ السِّنِينَ وَمَا بَلَغْنَا مَرَامًا بَلِ ازْدَدْنَا هَمًّا وَغَمًّا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥaḍarū qāla lahumu iʿlamū annanā aqamnā hādhihi al-sinīna wa-mā balaghnā marāman bali izdadnā hamman wa-ghamman
sentences.l: And when they were present he said to them: Know that we have stayed these years, and we have not reached an aim; rather we have increased in care and grief.
sentences.i: When they had come, he said to them, “You know that we have stayed here all these years and achieved nothing we aimed at; we have only gained more care and grief.
sentences.n: marām, “aim, object of desire”. hamm wa-ghamm, “care and grief”, a rhyming pair.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَتَيْنَا لِنَخْلُصَ مِنْ ثَأْرِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ فَقُتِلَ مِنَّا أَخِي شَرْكَانُ فَصَارَتِ الْحَسْرَةُ حَسْرَتَيْنِ وَالْمُصِيبَةُ مُصِيبَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ataynā li-nakhluṣa min thaʾri al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni fa-qutila minnā akhī sharrukānu fa-ṣārati al-ḥasratu ḥasratayni wa-al-muṣībatu muṣībatayni
sentences.l: And we came to get-clear of the blood-vengeance of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and there was killed of us my brother Sharrukān, so the sorrow became two sorrows, and the calamity two calamities.
sentences.i: We came here to be quit of the debt of vengeance for King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and instead my brother Sharrukān has been killed from among us; so our sorrow is doubled, and our calamity twice what it was.
sentences.n: thaʾr, “blood-vengeance”, is printed ثار without its hamza, as throughout. li-nakhluṣa min thaʾri, “to come clear of the vengeance”, i.e. to settle it by taking it; one might also read li-nukhalliṣa, “to exact”, but the min favours the reading given. qutila, “was killed”, is read as a passive.

sentences.t: وَسَبَبُ هٰذَا كُلِّهِ الْعَجُوزُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي فَإِنَّهَا هِىَ الَّتِي قَتَلَتِ السُّلْطَانَ فِي مَمْلَكَتِهِ وَأَخَذَتْ زَوْجَتَهُ الْمَلِكَةَ صَفِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: wa-sababu hādhā kullihi al-ʿajūzu dhātu al-dawāhī fa-innahā hiya allatī qatalati al-sulṭāna fī mamlakatihi wa-akhadhat zawjatahu al-malikata ṣafiyyata
sentences.l: And the cause of all this (is) the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, for she is the one who killed the sultan in his kingdom and took his wife, Queen Ṣafiyya.
sentences.i: And the cause of all this is the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī: it was she who killed the sultan in his own realm and carried off his wife, Queen Ṣafiyya.
sentences.n: The sultan is King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, whom she poisoned in his palace. Dhāt al-Dawāhī, “Mistress of Calamities”. The print marks the doubled yāʾ of Ṣafiyya.

sentences.t: وَمَا كَفَاهَا ذٰلِكَ حَتَّى عَمِلَتِ الْحِيلَةَ عَلَيْنَا وَذَبَحَتْ أَخِي
sentences.tr: wa-mā kafāhā dhālika ḥattā ʿamilati al-ḥīlata ʿalaynā wa-dhabaḥat akhī
sentences.l: And that did not suffice her, until she worked the trick on us and slaughtered my brother.
sentences.i: And not content with that, she played her trick on us and cut my brother's throat.
sentences.n: mā kafāhā dhālika ḥattā, “that was not enough for her, but she must also …”. ʿamila al-ḥīla ʿalā, “to work a stratagem against”.

sentences.t: وَقَدِ الْتَزَمْتُ وَحَلَفْتُ بِالْأَيْمَانِ الْعَظِيمَةِ أَنَّهُ لَا بُدَّ مِنْ أَخْذِ الثَّأْرِ فَمَا أَنْتُمْ قَائِلُونَ فَافْهَمُوا هٰذَا الْخِطَابَ وَرُدُّوا عَلَيَّ الْجَوَابَ
sentences.tr: wa-qadi iltazamtu wa-ḥalaftu bi-al-aymāni al-ʿaẓīmati annahu lā budda min akhdhi al-thaʾri fa-mā antum qāʾilūna fa-ifhamū hādhā al-khiṭāba wa-ruddū ʿalayya al-jawāba
sentences.l: And I have bound-myself and sworn by the great oaths that there is no escape from the taking of the vengeance. So what (are) you saying? Understand this address and return to me the answer.
sentences.i: I have pledged myself, and sworn the most solemn oaths, that vengeance must be taken. So what do you say? Consider what I have told you, and give me your answer.”
sentences.n: aymān, “oaths”, plural of yamīn, not īmān, “faith”: the two are spelt alike unpointed. lā budda min, “there is no getting out of”, i.e. it must be. The rhyme falls on al-khiṭāb … al-jawāb. The print itself marks the ending of iltazamtu and ḥalaftu, and the doubled dāl of ruddū and yāʾ of ʿalayya.

sentences.t: فَأَطْرَقُوا رُؤُسَهُمْ وَقَالُوا الرَّأْيُ لِلْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-aṭraqū ruʾūsahum wa-qālū al-raʾyu li-al-wazīri dandāna
sentences.l: And they lowered their heads and said: The counsel (belongs) to the vizier Dandān.
sentences.i: They bowed their heads and said, “The counsel belongs to the vizier Dandān.”
sentences.n: aṭraqa raʾsahu, “to bow the head” in thought or silence. The print spells ruʾūs, “heads”, with a single wāw (رؤسهم). li-, “belonging to”: it is for Dandān to advise.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ تَقَدَّمَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَقَالَ لَهُ اعْلَمْ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ أَنَّهُ مَا بَقِيَ فِي إِقَامَتِنَا فَائِدَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqaddama al-wazīru dandānu ilā al-maliki ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-qāla lahu iʿlam yā malika al-zamāni annahu mā baqiya fī iqāmatinā fāʾidatun
sentences.l: And at that, the vizier Dandān stepped forward to King Ḍawʾ al-Makān and said to him: Know, O king of the age, that there no longer remains in our staying a benefit.
sentences.i: At that the vizier Dandān came forward to King Ḍawʾ al-Makān and said to him, “Know, O king of the age, that there is no longer any use in our staying here.
sentences.n: mā baqiya, “there no longer remains”: baqiya with a negative is “no longer”. annahu, “that it (is so)”, the pronoun of the fact, introducing the clause.

sentences.t: وَالرَّأْىُ أَنَّنَا نَرْحَلُ إِلَى الْأَوْطَانِ وَنُقِيمُ هُنَاكَ بُرْهَةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ ثُمَّ نَعُودُ وَنَغْزُو عَبَدَةَ الْأَوْثَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-raʾyu annanā narḥalu ilā al-awṭāni wa-nuqīmu hunāka burhatan mina al-zamāni thumma naʿūdu wa-naghzū ʿabadata al-awthāni
sentences.l: And the counsel (is) that we depart to the homelands and stay there a while of the time, then return and raid the worshippers of the idols.
sentences.i: My counsel is that we go back to our homelands and stay there for a time, and then return and make war on the idol-worshippers.”
sentences.n: Rhyming prose again: al-awṭān … al-zamān … al-awthān. burha, “a space of time, a while”. ghazā, “to raid, to make war on (the infidel)”. ʿabadat al-awthān, “worshippers of idols”, the Christians of the story; the print itself puts the fatḥa on the ʿayn of ʿabada.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ نِعْمَ هٰذَا الرَّأْيُ لِأَنَّ النَّاسَ اشْتَاقُوا إِلَى رُؤْيَةِ عِيَالِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku niʿma hādhā al-raʾyu li-anna al-nāsa ishtāqū ilā ruʾyati ʿiyālihim
sentences.l: And the king said: Excellent (is) this counsel, because the people have longed for the sight of their families.
sentences.i: The king said, “That is good counsel, for the men are longing to see their families.
sentences.n: niʿma, “how excellent!”, the verb of praise; the print gives it its kasra. ʿiyāl, “dependants, wife and children”.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا الْآخَرُ أَيْضًا قَدْ أَقْلَقَنِي الشَّوْقُ إِلَى وَلَدِي كَانَ مَا كَانَ وَإِلَى ابْنَةِ أَخِي قَضَى فَكَانَ لِأَنَّهَا فِي دِمَشْقَ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-anā al-ākharu ayḍan qad aqlaqanī al-shawqu ilā waladī kāna mā kāna wa-ilā ibnati akhī qaḍā fakāna li-annahā fī dimashqa wa-lā aʿlamu mā kāna min amrihā
sentences.l: And I, the other, also: the longing has disquieted me for my son Kān Mā Kān, and for the daughter of my brother, Qaḍā Fakān, because she (is) in Damascus and I do not know what has been of her affair.
sentences.i: And I too am troubled with longing for my son Kān Mā Kān, and for my brother's daughter Qaḍā Fakān, for she is in Damascus and I do not know how she fares.”
sentences.n: anā al-ākhar, “I the other”, is spoken usage for “I too”, and ayḍan, “also”, says it again. Sharrukān's daughter is named here for the first time in the night: Qaḍā Fakān, “He decreed, and it came to be”, a pair with her cousin's name Kān Mā Kān, “What was, was”; it could also be read Quḍiya Fakān, “It was decreed, and it came to be”. mā kāna min amrihā, “what has become of her”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ الْعَسَاكِرُ ذٰلِكَ فَرِحُوا وَدَعَوْا لِلْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-ʿasākiru dhālika fariḥū wa-daʿaw li-al-wazīri dandāna
sentences.l: And when the troops heard that, they rejoiced and prayed for the vizier Dandān.
sentences.i: When the troops heard this they were glad, and called down blessings on the vizier Dandān.
sentences.n: daʿā li-, “to pray for, bless”; daʿā ʿalā would be “to curse”. The verb is feminine singular before the plural al-ʿasākir, then the sense takes over and the next verbs are masculine plural.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ أَمَرَ الْمُنَادِيَ أَنْ يُنَادِيَ بِالرَّحِيلِ بَعْدَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika ḍawʾa al-makāni amara al-munādiya an yunādiya bi-al-raḥīli baʿda thalāthati ayyāmin
sentences.l: Then King Ḍawʾ al-Makān commanded the crier that he cry the departure after three days.
sentences.i: Then King Ḍawʾ al-Makān ordered the crier to proclaim that they would march in three days' time.
sentences.n: nādā bi-, “to proclaim”: bi- names what is cried out. The print spells thalātha without its long alif (ثلٰثة) and marks it with the small alif itself.

sentences.t: فَابْتَدَؤُا فِي تَجْهِيزِ أَحْوَالِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ibtadaʾū fī tajhīzi aḥwālihim
sentences.l: And they began in the readying of their affairs.
sentences.i: So they set about getting their things ready.
sentences.n: The print spells ibtadaʾū with the hamza on a wāw seat and no second wāw (فابتدؤا). aḥwāl, “circumstances, affairs”, here their gear and baggage.

sentences.t: وَفِى الْيَوْمِ الرَّابِعِ دُقَّتِ الْكَاسَاتُ وَنُشِرَتِ الرَّايَاتُ وَتَقَدَّمَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ فِي مُقَدَّمِ الْعَسْكَرِ وَسَارَ الْمَلِكُ فِي وَسَطِهِ وَبِجَانِبِهِ الْحَاجِبُ الْكَبِيرُ
sentences.tr: wa-fī al-yawmi al-rābiʿi duqqati al-kāsātu wa-nushirati al-rāyātu wa-taqaddama al-wazīru dandānu fī muqaddami al-ʿaskari wa-sāra al-maliku fī wasaṭihi wa-bi-jānibihi al-ḥājibu al-kabīru
sentences.l: And on the day the fourth, the kettledrums were beaten and the banners were spread, and the vizier Dandān went-forward in the front of the army, and the king went in its middle, and at his side the Great Chamberlain.
sentences.i: On the fourth day the kettledrums were beaten and the banners unfurled. The vizier Dandān rode at the head of the army, and the king in its midst, with the Great Chamberlain beside him.
sentences.n: The print has دنّت, a misprint for دقّت, corrected here; the print's shadda stands on the corrected word. kāsāt, plural of kāsa, “bowl”, here the bowl-shaped kettledrums of the army. The print marks the doubled dāl of taqaddama. muqaddam al-ʿaskar, “the van of the army”.

sentences.t: وَسَارَتِ الْجُيُوشُ وَمَا زَالُوا سَائِرِينَ فِى اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا إِلَى مَدِينَةِ بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: wa-sārati al-juyūshu wa-mā zālū sāʾirīna fī al-layli wa-al-nahāri ḥattā waṣalū ilā madīnati baghdāda
sentences.l: And the armies went, and they did not cease journeying in the night and the day until they arrived at the city of Baghdad.
sentences.i: The armies marched, and they travelled on night and day until they reached the city of Baghdad.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَتْ بِقُدُومِهِمُ النَّاسُ وَزَالَ عَنْهُمُ الْهَمُّ وَالْبَأْسُ وَالْتَقَتِ الْحُضَّارُ بِالْغُيَّابِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥat bi-qudūmihimu al-nāsu wa-zāla ʿanhumu al-hammu wa-al-baʾsu wa-iltaqati al-ḥuḍḍāru bi-al-ghuyyābi
sentences.l: And the people rejoiced at their arrival, and there departed from them the care and the distress, and the present-ones met with the absent-ones.
sentences.i: The people rejoiced at their coming; care and hardship left them, and those who had stayed at home were united with those who had been away.
sentences.n: The rhyme falls on al-nās … al-baʾs, which the print spells without its hamza (الباس), so that in reading it chimes bās with nās. baʾs, “hardship, distress”. ḥuḍḍār, “those present”, the stay-at-homes, and ghuyyāb, “the absent”; the print marks both doubled letters. iltaqā bi-, “to meet with”.

sentences.t: وَذَهَبَ كُلُّ أَمِيرٍ إِلَى دَارِهِ وَطَلَعَ الْمَلِكُ إِلَى قَصْرِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-dhahaba kullu amīrin ilā dārihi wa-ṭalaʿa al-maliku ilā qaṣrihi
sentences.l: And each emir went to his house, and the king went-up to his palace.
sentences.i: Every emir went off to his own house, and the king went up to his palace.
sentences.n: ṭalaʿa ilā, “to go up to”, the usual verb in the Nights for going to the palace or the citadel.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ عَلَى وَلَدِهِ كَانَ مَا كَانَ وَقَدْ بَلَغَ مِنَ الْعُمْرِ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ وَصَارَ يَنْزِلُ وَيَرْكَبُ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala ʿalā waladihi kāna mā kāna wa-qad balagha mina al-ʿumri sabʿa sinīna wa-ṣāra yanzilu wa-yarkabu
sentences.l: And he went in to his son Kān Mā Kān, and he had reached of age seven years, and had become (one who) dismounts and mounts.
sentences.i: He went in to his son Kān Mā Kān, who was now seven years old and already riding about on his own.
sentences.n: ṣāra yanzilu wa-yarkabu, “he had begun to dismount and mount”: he could get on and off a horse, i.e. he could ride. ṣāra with an imperfect is “to begin to, come to”.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا اسْتَرَاحَ الْمَلِكُ مِنَ السَّفَرِ دَخَلَ الْحَمَّامَ هُوَ وَوَلَدُهُ كَانَ مَا كَانَ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ وَجَلَسَ عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ مَمْلَكَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā istarāḥa al-maliku mina al-safari dakhala al-ḥammāma huwa wa-waladuhu kāna mā kāna thumma rajaʿa wa-jalasa ʿalā kursiyyi mamlakatihi
sentences.l: And when the king had rested from the journey, he entered the bath, he and his son Kān Mā Kān; then he returned and sat on the chair of his kingdom.
sentences.i: When the king had rested from his journey, he went to the bath with his son Kān Mā Kān, and then came back and took his seat on the throne of his kingdom.

sentences.t: وَوَقَفَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَطَلَعَتِ الْأُمَرَاءُ وَخَوَاصُّ الدَّوْلَةِ وَوَقَفُوا فِي خِدْمَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-waqafa al-wazīru dandānu bayna yadayhi wa-ṭalaʿati al-umarāʾu wa-khawāṣṣu al-dawlati wa-waqafū fī khidmatihi
sentences.l: And the vizier Dandān stood between his two hands, and the emirs and the special-ones of the state came-up and stood in his service.
sentences.i: The vizier Dandān stood before him, and the emirs and the chief men of the state came up and stood in attendance on him.
sentences.n: bayna yadayhi, “between his hands”, before him. khawāṣṣ al-dawla, “the intimates of the state”, the great officers about the king. fī khidmatihi, “in his service”, waiting on him.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ طَلَبَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ صَاحِبَهُ الْوَقَّادَ الَّذِي كَانَ أَحْسَنَ إِلَيْهِ فِي غُرْبَتِهِ فَاُحْضِرَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ṭalaba ḍawʾu al-makāni ṣāḥibahu al-waqqāda alladhī kāna aḥsana ilayhi fī ghurbatihi fa-uḥḍira
sentences.l: And at that, Ḍawʾ al-Makān asked for his friend the stoker, who had done-good to him in his strangerhood, and he was brought.
sentences.i: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān sent for his friend the stoker, who had been kind to him when he was a stranger far from home, and he was brought.
sentences.n: The waqqād is the stoker of the bath-house in Jerusalem who took Ḍawʾ al-Makān in when he was sick and destitute. aḥsana ilā, “to do good to”. ghurba, “being far from home, exile”. The print itself puts the ḍamma on the alif of uḥḍira, marking it as a passive.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَضَرَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ قَامَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ إِعْظَامًا لِحَقِّهِ وَأَجْلَسَهُ إِلَى جَانِبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥaḍara bayna yadayhi qāma lahu al-maliku iʿẓāman li-ḥaqqihi wa-ajlasahu ilā jānibihi
sentences.l: And when he was present between his hands, the king rose for him, in magnifying of his due, and seated him at his side.
sentences.i: When he stood before him, the king rose to his feet for him, to honour what he owed him, and seated him at his side.
sentences.n: iʿẓāman li-ḥaqqihi, “out of reverence for his claim”: ḥaqq is what the stoker had earned by his kindness. The print marks the doubled qāf.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْمَلِكُ قَدْ حَدَّثَ لِلْوَزِيرِ بِمَا فَعَلَهُ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ وَالْمَعْرُوفِ فَعَظَّمَتْهُ الْأُمَرَاءُ وَعَظَّمَهُ الْوَزِيرُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-maliku qad ḥaddatha li-al-wazīri bi-mā faʿalahu maʿahu mina al-khayri wa-al-maʿrūfi fa-ʿaẓẓamathu al-umarāʾu wa-ʿaẓẓamahu al-wazīru
sentences.l: And the king had told to the vizier of what he had done with him of the good and the kindness; so the emirs honoured him, and the vizier honoured him.
sentences.i: The king had told the vizier of all the good and kindness the man had shown him, and so the emirs did him honour, and so did the vizier.
sentences.n: The print has للوزبر, a misprint for للوزير, and then الوزبر, a misprint for الوزير; both are corrected here. ḥaddatha li-, “to tell to”: Classical ḥaddatha takes the person told directly, and the li- is the spoken usage; bi- names what is told. faʿala maʿahu, “did with him”, i.e. did for him. The print marks the doubled dāl and ẓāʾ.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْوَقَّادُ قَدْ غَلُظَ وَسَمِنَ مِنَ الْأَكْلِ وَالرَّاحَةِ وَصَارَ عُنُقُهُ كَعُنُقِ الْفِيلِ وَوَجْهُهُ كَبَطْنِ الدُّرْفِيلِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-waqqādu qad ghaluẓa wa-samina mina al-akli wa-al-rāḥati wa-ṣāra ʿunuquhu ka-ʿunuqi al-fīli wa-wajhuhu ka-baṭni al-durfīli
sentences.l: And the stoker had grown-thick and grown-fat from the eating and the ease, and his neck had become like the neck of the elephant, and his face like the belly of the dolphin.
sentences.i: The stoker had grown stout and fat from good eating and idleness: his neck had become like an elephant's, and his face like a dolphin's belly.
sentences.n: The comic rhyme falls on al-fīl … al-durfīl. durfīl is a by-form of dulfīn, “dolphin”, shaped here to chime with fīl; the point is a face broad, pale and puffy. ghaluẓa, “to grow thick, coarse”.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ طَأئِشَ الْعَقْلِ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْمَكَانِ الَّذِي هُوَ فِيهِ فَلَمْ يَعْرِفِ الْمَلِكَ بِسِيمَاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra ṭāʾisha al-ʿaqli li-annahu kāna lā yakhruju mina al-makāni alladhī huwa fīhi fa-lam yaʿrifi al-malika bi-sīmāhu
sentences.l: And he had become flighty of the mind, because he would not go out from the place in which he (was), so he did not know the king by his mark.
sentences.i: And he had become feather-brained, because he never left the place where he lived; so he did not recognise the king by his looks.
sentences.n: ṭāʾish al-ʿaql, “light of mind, giddy”: the print spells ṭāʾish oddly, with a hamza on the alif and another on the yāʾ seat (طأئش). sīmā, “mark, mien, look”. The stoker does not know the king; the king, as the next words show, knows him.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْمَلِكُ وَانْبَشَّ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَحَيَّاهُ أَعْظَمَ التَّحِيَّاتِ وَقَالَ لَهُ مَا أَسْرَعَ مَانَسِيتَنِي
sentences.tr: fa-aqbala ʿalayhi al-maliku wa-inbashsha fī wajhihi wa-ḥayyāhu aʿẓama al-taḥiyyāti wa-qāla lahu mā asraʿa mā nasītanī
sentences.l: And the king came-towards him, and was cheerful in his face, and greeted him the greatest of greetings, and said to him: How quick (is) that you forgot me!
sentences.i: The king turned to him with a beaming face, greeted him with every mark of honour, and said to him, “How quickly you have forgotten me!
sentences.n: aqbala ʿalā, “to turn towards, give one's attention to”. inbashsha, form VII of bashsha, “to be cheerful, smile on”, a form of the spoken language; fī wajhihi, “in his face”, towards him. The print marks the doubled shīn of inbashsha and yāʾ of ḥayyāhu. mā asraʿa mā nasītanī, “how quick was your forgetting me!”, the exclamation mā afʿala; the print runs mā nasītanī together (مانسيتني).

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ تَنَبَّهَ الْوَقَّادُ فَأَمْعَنَ فِيهِ النَّظَرَ وَتَحَقَّقَهُ فَعَرَفَهُ وَقَامَ وَاثِبًا عَلَى الْأَقْدَامِ وَقَالَ يَا حَبِيبِي مَنِ الَّذِي عَمِلَكَ سُلْطَانًا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika tanabbaha al-waqqādu fa-amʿana fīhi al-naẓara wa-taḥaqqaqahu fa-ʿarafahu wa-qāma wāthiban ʿalā al-aqdāmi wa-qāla yā ḥabībī mani alladhī ʿamilaka sulṭānan
sentences.l: And at that the stoker woke-up, and he pressed the gaze deep into him and made-sure-of him, and he knew him, and rose leaping onto the feet, and said: O my dear, who is it that made you a sultan?
sentences.i: At that the stoker came to his senses. He looked at him long and hard, made sure of him and knew him; he sprang to his feet and said, “My dear friend, who made you a sultan?”
sentences.n: amʿana al-naẓara fīhi, “to make the look go deep into someone”: to scrutinise. ʿamilaka sulṭānan, “made you a sultan”: ʿamila, “to do”, used for “to make (someone something)” is the spoken idiom. The print marks the doubled bāʾ of tanabbaha and the doubled qāf of taḥaqqaqahu.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And he laughed at him.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān laughed at him.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْوَزِيرُ وَشَرَحَ لَهُ الْقِصَّةَ وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ أَخَاكَ وَصَاحِبَكَ وَالْآنَ صَارَ مَلِكَ الْأَرْضِ وَلَابُدَّأَنْ يَصِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْهُ خَيْرٌ كَثِيرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbala ʿalayhi al-wazīru wa-sharaḥa lahu al-qiṣṣata wa-qāla lahu innahu kāna akhāka wa-ṣāḥibaka wa-al-āna ṣāra malika al-arḍi wa-lā budda an yaṣila ilayka minhu khayrun kathīrun
sentences.l: And the vizier came-forward to him and explained to him the story, and said to him: He was your brother and your companion, and now he has become king of the earth, and there is no escape from that much good reach you from him.
sentences.i: Then the vizier came up to him and explained the whole story. “He was your brother and your friend,” he said, “and now he has become king of the world; you are bound to get a great deal of good from him.
sentences.n: lā budda an, “there is no escape from…”, i.e. “it must be that…”, is run together in the print (ولابدان). The print writes al-āna with its madda (الآن).

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا أُوصِيكَ إِذَا قَالَ لَكَ تَمَنَّ عَلَيَّ فَلَا تَتَمَنَّ إِلَّا شَيْأً عَظِيمًا لِأَنَّكَ عِنْدَهُ عَزِيزٌ
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā ūṣīka idhā qāla laka tamanna ʿalayya fa-lā tatamanna illā shayʾan ʿaẓīman li-annaka ʿindahu ʿazīzun
sentences.l: And here I am advising you: if he says to you, ‘Wish upon me’, then do not wish anything but a great thing, because you are dear with him.
sentences.i: Now here is my advice to you: if he says to you, ‘Make a wish of me’, wish for nothing but something great, for he holds you dear.”
sentences.n: tamannā ʿalā, “to wish upon (someone)”: to name a wish for someone to grant. shayʾan, “a thing”, is printed شيأ, with the hamza on an alif, as the print often spells it. The print marks the doubled nūn of tamanna and tatamanna, the doubled yāʾ of ʿalayya and the doubled lām of illā.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَقَّادُ أَخَافُ أَنْ أَتَمَنَّيٰ عَلَيْهِ شَيْأً فَلَا يَسْمَحَ لِي بِهِ أَوْلَا يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-waqqādu akhāfu an atamannā ʿalayhi shayʾan fa-lā yasmaḥa lī bihi aw lā yaqdira ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And the stoker said: I fear that I wish upon him a thing, and he not grant it to me, or not be able for it.
sentences.i: The stoker said, “I am afraid I shall wish for something and he will not let me have it, or will not be able to give it.”
sentences.n: The print writes atamannā with final ي for ى (اتمنّي), and runs aw lā together (اولا). samaḥa li-… bi-, “to grant someone something”, to be generous with it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ كُلَّمَا تَمَنَّيْتَهُ يُعْطِيكَ إِيَّاهُ وَمَا عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru kullamā tamannaytahu yuʿṭīka iyyāhu wa-mā ʿalayka shayʾun
sentences.l: And the vizier said to him: Whatever you wish it, he gives you it; and there is nothing upon you.
sentences.i: The vizier said to him, “Whatever you wish for, he will give you; you have nothing to worry about.”
sentences.n: kullamā, normally “whenever”, stands here for kull mā, “all that, whatever”, as it often does in this text. mā ʿalayka shayʾun, “nothing is upon you”: no blame or risk falls on you. The print marks the doubled nūn of tamannaytahu.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ وَاللّٰهِ لَابُدَّ أَنِّي سَأَتَمَنَّيٰ عَلَيْهِ الشَّيْءَ الَّذِي فِي خَاطِرِي وَكُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ أَحْلُمُ بِهِ وَأَرْجُو مِنَ اللّٰهِ تَعَالَى أَنْ يَسْمَحَ لِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu wa-allāhi lā budda annī sa-atamannā ʿalayhi al-shayʾa alladhī fī khāṭirī wa-kulla laylatin aḥlumu bihi wa-arjū mina allāhi taʿālā an yasmaḥa lī bihi
sentences.l: And he said to him: By God, there is no escape (from it) that I shall wish upon him the thing which (is) in my mind, and every night I dream of it, and I hope from God (the) Exalted that he grant it to me.
sentences.i: He said, “By God, then I shall certainly wish for the thing I have in mind. I dream of it every night, and I pray to God Most High that he will grant it to me.”
sentences.n: lā budda annī, “there is no escape (but) that I…”: the spoken language puts annī after lā budda where Classical has an with the subjunctive. khāṭir, “mind, thoughts”. Again atamannā is printed with final ي (ساتمنّي).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ طَيِّبْ قَلْبَكَ وَاللّٰهِ لَوْ طَلَبْتَ وِلَايَةَ دِمَشْقَ مَوْضِعَ أَخِيهِ لَأَعْطَاكَ وَوَلَّاكَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru ṭayyib qalbaka wa-allāhi law ṭalabta wilāyata dimashqa mawḍiʿa akhīhi la-aʿṭāka wa-wallāka ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And the vizier said to him: Make-good your heart! By God, if you asked (for) the governorship of Damascus in the place of his brother, he would give you (it) and set you over it.
sentences.i: “Set your heart at rest,” said the vizier. “By God, if you asked for the governorship of Damascus in his brother's place, he would give it to you and make you its ruler.”
sentences.n: The print has الوزبر, a misprint for الوزير, corrected here. ṭayyib qalbaka, “make your heart good”: be easy, cheer up. His brother is the late Sharrukān, who held Damascus. The print marks the doubled yāʾ of ṭayyib and the doubled lām of wallāka.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ قَامَ الْوَقَّادُ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ فَأَشَارَ لَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ أَنِ اجْلِسْ فَأَبَى وَقَالَ مَعَاذَ اللّٰهِ قَدِ انْقَضَتْ أَيَّامُ قُعُودِي فِي حَضْرَتِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qāma al-waqqādu ʿalā qadamayhi fa-ashāra lahu ḍawʾu al-makāni ani ijlis fa-abā wa-qāla maʿādha allāhi qadi inqaḍat ayyāmu quʿūdī fī ḥaḍratika
sentences.l: And at that the stoker stood on his two feet, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān signed to him: Sit! But he refused and said: Refuge of God! The days of my sitting in your presence have come-to-an-end.
sentences.i: At that the stoker got to his feet. Ḍawʾ al-Makān signed to him to sit, but he would not. “God forbid!” he said. “The days when I could sit in your presence are over.”
sentences.n: maʿādha allāhi, “(I seek) the refuge of God”: “God forbid!”. ḥaḍra, “presence”, is the courtly word for a great man's company.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ السُّلْطَانُ لَابَلْ هِيَ بَاقِيَةٌ إِلَى الْآنِ فَإِنَّكَ كُنْتَ سَبَبًا لِحَيَاتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-sulṭānu lā bal hiya bāqiyatun ilā al-āni fa-innaka kunta sababan li-ḥayātī
sentences.l: And the sultan said to him: No, rather they (are) remaining until now, for you were a cause of my life.
sentences.i: “No,” said the sultan, “they last to this day; for it was you who saved my life.”
sentences.n: The print has بانية, a misprint for باقية, corrected here. lā bal, “no, rather”, is run together in the print (لابل).

sentences.t: وَاللّٰهِ لَوْ طَلَبْتَ مِنِّي مَهْمَا أَرَدْتَ لَأَعْطَيْتُكَ إِيَّاهُ وَلٰكِنْ تَمَنَّ عَلَى اللّٰهِ ثُمَّ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: wa-allāhi law ṭalabta minnī mahmā aradta la-aʿṭaytuka iyyāhu wa-lākin tamanna ʿalā allāhi thumma ʿalayya
sentences.l: By God, if you asked of me whatever you wanted, I would give you it; but wish upon God, then upon me.
sentences.i: By God, whatever you asked of me, I would give it to you. So make your wish of God, and then of me.”
sentences.n: “Upon God, then upon me”: the wish is put first to God, the true giver, and then to the king; the stoker repeats the formula below. The print marks the doubled nūn of tamanna and the doubled yāʾ of ʿalayya.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَاسَيِّدِي إِنِّي أَخَافُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī innī akhāfu
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my lord, I am afraid.
sentences.i: “My lord,” he said, “I am afraid.”
sentences.n: yā sayyidī is run together in the print (ياسيدي).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَا تَخَفْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lā takhaf
sentences.l: And he said: Do not fear.
sentences.i: “Do not be afraid,” said the king.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخَافُ أَنْ أَتَمَنَّى شَيْأً فَلَا تَسْمَحَ لِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhāfu an atamannā shayʾan fa-lā tasmaḥa lī bihi
sentences.l: And he said: I fear that I wish a thing and you not grant it to me.
sentences.i: “I am afraid I shall wish for something and you will not let me have it.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَمَا هُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-mā huwa
sentences.l: And he said: And what is it?
sentences.i: “And what is it?” said the king.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ السُّلْطَانُ وَقَالَ لَهُ لَوْ تَمَنَّيْتُ نِصْفَ مَمْلَكَتِي لَشَارَكْتُكَ فِيهَا فَتَمَنَّ مَا تُرِيدُ وَدَعِ الْكَلَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-sulṭānu wa-qāla lahu law tamannaytu niṣfa mamlakatī la-shāraktuka fīhā fa-tamanna mā turīdu wa-daʿi al-kalāma
sentences.l: And the sultan laughed and said to him: If I wished half my kingdom, I would share you in it; so wish what you want and leave the talk.
sentences.i: The sultan laughed and said, “If you wished for half my kingdom, I would share it with you. So wish for what you like, and enough of this talk.”
sentences.n: The print points law tamannaytu, “if I wished”, in the first person; the sense asks for tamannayta, “if you wished”, and the idiomatic rendering follows the sense. The print's damma is kept. shārakahu fī, “to make someone a partner in”.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْوَقَّادُ أَخَافُ
sentences.tr: qāla al-waqqādu akhāfu
sentences.l: The stoker said: I am afraid.
sentences.i: “I am afraid,” said the stoker.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَاتَخَفْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lā takhaf
sentences.l: And he said: Do not fear.
sentences.i: “Do not be afraid,” said the king.
sentences.n: lā takhaf is run together in the print here (لاتخف).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخَافُ أَنْ أَتَمَنَّى شَيْأً لَاتَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhāfu an atamannā shayʾan lā taqdiru ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And he said: I fear that I wish a thing you are not able for.
sentences.i: “I am afraid I shall wish for something beyond your power.”
sentences.n: lā taqdiru is run together in the print (لاتقدر).

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ غَضِبَ السُّلْطَانُ وَقَالَ لَهُ تَمَنَّ مَا أَرَدْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ghaḍiba al-sulṭānu wa-qāla lahu tamanna mā aradta
sentences.l: And at that the sultan grew-angry and said to him: Wish what you wanted!
sentences.i: At this the sultan lost his temper and said, “Wish for whatever you want!”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَتَمَنَّى عَلَيٰ اللّٰهِ ثُمَّ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَكْتُبَ لِي مَرْسُومًا بِعِرَافَةِ جَمِيعِ الْوَقَّادِينَ الَّذِينَ بِمَدِينَةِ الْقُدْسِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu atamannā ʿalā allāhi thumma ʿalayka an taktuba lī marsūman bi-ʿirāfati jamīʿi al-waqqādīna alladhīna bi-madīnati al-qudsi
sentences.l: And he said to him: I wish upon God, then upon you, that you write for me a decree with the headship of all the stokers who (are) in the city of Jerusalem.
sentences.i: He said, “I wish of God, and then of you, that you write me a decree making me headman of all the stokers in the city of Jerusalem.”
sentences.n: marsūm, “a decree, a patent of appointment”; bi-, “with”, gives what the decree confers. ʿirāfa is the office of the ʿarīf, the overseer of a trade or a quarter. ʿalā is printed with ي (علي).

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ السُّلْطَانُ وَجَمِيعُ مَنْ حَضَرَ وَقَالَ لَهُ تَمَنَّ غَيْرَ هٰذَا
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-sulṭānu wa-jamīʿu man ḥaḍara wa-qāla lahu tamanna ghayra hādhā
sentences.l: And the sultan laughed, and all who were present, and he said to him: Wish other than this.
sentences.i: The sultan laughed, and so did everyone there, and he said, “Wish for something else.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَاسَيِّدِى أَنَا مَا قُلْتُ لَكَ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ أَتَمَنَّى شَيْأً لَا تَسْمَحُ لِي بِهِ أَوْلَا تَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidī anā mā qultu laka innī akhāfu an atamannā shayʾan lā tasmaḥu lī bihi aw lā taqdiru ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And he said: O my lord, I, did I not say to you that I fear that I wish a thing you will not grant me, or are not able for?
sentences.i: “My lord,” he said, “didn't I tell you I was afraid I would wish for something you would not grant me, or could not give?”
sentences.n: anā mā qultu laka, “I, did I not tell you?”: the spoken “I told you so”, the question carried by the tone. The print writes sayyidī with final ى (ياسيدى) and runs aw lā together (اولا).

sentences.t: فَلَكَزَهُ الْوَزِيرُ ثَانِيًا وَثَالِثًا وَفِي كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ يَقُولُ أَتَمَنَّى عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lakazahu al-wazīru thāniyan wa-thālithan wa-fī kulli marratin yaqūlu atamannā ʿalayka
sentences.l: And the vizier jabbed him a second and a third (time), and at every time he says: I wish upon you…
sentences.i: The vizier dug him in the ribs a second time and a third, and each time he only said, “I wish of you…”
sentences.n: lakaza, “to strike with the fist, to jab”. thāniyan wa-thālithan, “a second and a third (time)”: the first jab is not told; it must have come with the wish about the stokers.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ السُّلْطَانُ تَمَنَّ وَأَسْرِعْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-sulṭānu tamanna wa-asriʿ
sentences.l: And the sultan said to him: Wish, and be quick!
sentences.i: “Wish,” said the sultan, “and be quick about it!”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَتَمَنَّى عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَجْعَلَنِي رَئِيسَ الزَّبَّالِينَ فِي مَدِينَةِ الْقُدْسِ أَوْفِي مَدِينَةِ دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla atamannā ʿalayka an tajʿalanī raʾīsa al-zabbālīna fī madīnati al-qudsi aw fī madīnati dimashqa
sentences.l: And he said: I wish upon you that you make me chief of the dung-men in the city of Jerusalem, or in the city of Damascus.
sentences.i: He said, “I wish of you that you make me chief of the dung-collectors in the city of Jerusalem, or else in the city of Damascus.”
sentences.n: zabbāl, from zibl, “dung”, is the man who gathers dung and refuse, which was dried and burned as fuel for the bath-house furnaces: a stoker's natural next step up. aw fī is run together in the print (اوفي).

sentences.t: فَانْقَلَبَ الْحَاضِرُونَ عَلَى ظُهُورِهِمْ مِنَ الضَّحِكِ عَلَيْهِ وَضَرَبَهُ الْوَزِيرُ
sentences.tr: fa-inqalaba al-ḥāḍirūna ʿalā ẓuhūrihim mina al-ḍaḥiki ʿalayhi wa-ḍarabahu al-wazīru
sentences.l: And those present turned-over onto their backs from the laughing at him, and the vizier struck him.
sentences.i: Everyone there fell over backwards laughing at him, and the vizier hit him.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ الْوَقَّادُ إِلَى الْوَزِيرِ وَقَالَ لَهُ إِيشْ تَكُونُ حَتَّى تَضْرِبَنِي وَمَا لِي ذَنْبٌ فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الَّذِى قُلْتَ لِي تَمَنَّ شَيْأً عَظِيمًا
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata al-waqqādu ilā al-wazīri wa-qāla lahu īsh takūnu ḥattā taḍribanī wa-mā lī dhanbun fa-innaka anta alladhī qulta lī tamanna shayʾan ʿaẓīman
sentences.l: And the stoker turned to the vizier and said to him: What are you, that you should strike me, and I have no fault? For it is you who said to me: Wish a great thing.
sentences.i: The stoker turned to the vizier and said, “Who do you think you are, hitting me when I've done nothing wrong? It was you who told me to wish for something great!”
sentences.n: īsh, “what?”, is the spoken contraction of ayy shayʾ, “what thing?”. Here shayʾan is printed شياً, with the tanwīn marked on a bare alif. The print writes alladhī with final ى (الذى).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ دَعُونِي أَسِيرُ إِلَى بِلَادِى
sentences.tr: thumma qāla daʿūnī asīru ilā bilādī
sentences.l: Then he said: Let me go to my country.
sentences.i: Then he said, “Let me go back home.”
sentences.n: daʿūnī asīru, “leave me, I go”: the second verb follows without an, as in the spoken language. The print writes bilādī with final ى (بلادى).

sentences.t: فَعَرَفَ السُّلْطَانُ أَنَّهُ يَلْعَبُ فَصَبَرَ عَلَيْهِ قَلِيلًا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿarafa al-sulṭānu annahu yalʿabu fa-ṣabara ʿalayhi qalīlan
sentences.l: And the sultan knew that he was playing, and he bore with him a little.
sentences.i: The sultan saw that he was only joking, and was patient with him a while.
sentences.n: yalʿabu, “he is playing”: the sultan takes him to be fooling, not simple.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي تَمَنَّ عَلَيَّ شَيْأً عَظِيمًا لَائِقًا بِمَقَامِنَا
sentences.tr: thumma aqbala ʿalayhi wa-qāla lahu yā akhī tamanna ʿalayya shayʾan ʿaẓīman lāʾiqan bi-maqāminā
sentences.l: Then he turned-toward him and said to him: O my brother, wish upon me a great thing, fitting to our station.
sentences.i: Then he turned to him and said, “Brother, wish of me something great, something worthy of our rank.”
sentences.n: lāʾiq bi-, “befitting”. maqāminā, “our station”, the royal “we”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ إِنِّي أَتَمَنَّى عَلَى اللّٰهِ ثُمَّ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ أَنْ تُوَلِّيَنِي نَائِبَ دِمَشْقَ مَوْضِعَ أَخِيكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā malika al-zamāni innī atamannā ʿalā allāhi thumma ʿalā al-maliki an tuwalliyanī nāʾiba dimashqa mawḍiʿa akhīka
sentences.l: And he said: O king of the time, I wish upon God, then upon the king, that you appoint me viceroy of Damascus in the place of your brother.
sentences.i: He said, “King of the age, I wish of God, and then of the king, that you make me viceroy of Damascus in your brother's place.”
sentences.n: nāʾib, “deputy”: the governor who rules a province in the sultan's name. He speaks of “the king” in the third person and then turns to “you”, as courtesy allows.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ إِنَّ اللّٰهَ أَعْطَاكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku inna allāha aʿṭāka
sentences.l: And the king said: God has given you (it).
sentences.i: “God has granted it to you,” said the king.
sentences.n: inna allāha aʿṭāka, “God has given you”: the wish is granted in the same terms it was asked, God first.

sentences.t: فَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ بِوَضْعِ كُرْسِيٍّ لَهُ فِي مَرْتَبَتِهِ وَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ خِلْعَةَ النِّيَابَةِ وَكَتَبَ لَهُ التَّوْقِيعَ بِذٰلِكَ وَخَتَمَهُ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-amara al-maliku bi-waḍʿi kursiyyin lahu fī martabatihi wa-khalaʿa ʿalayhi khilʿata al-niyābati wa-kataba lahu al-tawqīʿa bi-dhālika wa-khatamahu lahu
sentences.l: And he kissed the ground between his two hands, and the king commanded the placing of a chair for him in his rank, and robed him in the robe of the viceroyalty, and wrote for him the warrant for that and sealed it for him.
sentences.i: He kissed the ground before him; and the king ordered a chair to be set for him in the place his rank required, invested him with the robe of a viceroy, wrote out his warrant of appointment and sealed it for him.
sentences.n: amara bi-, “to order (something)”: the verb takes its object with bi-. khalaʿa ʿalayhi khilʿatan, “to put a robe of honour on someone”, the sign of appointment. tawqīʿ, “signature”, here the signed warrant. The print marks the doubled bāʾ of qabbala.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِلْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ مَايَرُوحُ مَعَهُ غَيْرُكَ وَإِذَا أَرَدْتَ الْعَوْدَ وَجِئْتَ فَأَحْضِرْ مَعَكَ ابْنَةَ أَخِي قَضَى فَكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-al-wazīri dandāna mā yarūḥu maʿahu ghayruka wa-idhā aradta al-ʿawda wa-jiʾta fa-aḥḍir maʿaka ibnata akhī qaḍā fakāna
sentences.l: And he said to the vizier Dandān: There goes not with him other than you; and when you want the return and come, then bring with you my brother's daughter Qaḍā Fakān.
sentences.i: And he said to the vizier Dandān, “No one shall go with him but you; and when you mean to come back, bring my brother's daughter Qaḍā Fakān with you.”
sentences.n: rāḥa, “to go”, is the spoken verb; mā yarūḥu is run together in the print (مايروح).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And the vizier said: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: The vizier answered with hearing and obedience.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَ الْوَقَّادَ وَنَزَلَ بِهِ وَتَجَهَّزَ لِلسَّفَرِ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadha al-waqqāda wa-nazala bihi wa-tajahhaza li-al-safari
sentences.l: Then he took the stoker and went-down with him, and made-ready for the journey.
sentences.i: Then he took the stoker, went down with him from the palace, and made ready for the journey.
sentences.n: nazala bihi, “went down with him”: from the citadel, where the king sits, into the town. The print marks the doubled hāʾ of tajahhaza.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ أَنْ يُخْرِجُوا لِلْوَقَّادِ خَدَمًا وَحَشَمًا وَتَخْتًا جَدِيدًا وَطَقْمَ سَلْطَنَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-amara al-maliku an yukhrijū li-al-waqqādi khadaman wa-ḥashaman wa-takhtan jadīdan wa-ṭaqma salṭanatin
sentences.l: And the king commanded that they bring out for the stoker servants and retinue, and a new throne, and a set of sovereignty.
sentences.i: The king ordered servants and attendants to be produced for the stoker, and a new throne, and the full regalia of royal state.
sentences.n: takht, a Persian word, “throne” or “couch of state”. ṭaqm, “a set, a full outfit” (Turkish takım), a late word; ṭaqm salṭana is everything that goes with sovereign state.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِلْأُمَرَاءِ مَنْ كَانَ يُحِبُّنِي فَلْيُكْرِمْ هٰذَا وَيُقَدِّمْ لَهُ هَدِيَّةً عَظِيمَةً
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-al-umarāʾi man kāna yuḥibbunī fa-l-yukrim hādhā wa-yuqaddim lahu hadiyyatan ʿaẓīmatan
sentences.l: And he said to the emirs: Whoever loves me, let him honour this (one) and present to him a great gift.
sentences.i: And he said to the emirs, “Whoever loves me, let him do this man honour and offer him a handsome gift.”
sentences.n: fa-l-yukrim, “then let him honour”: the li- of command loses its vowel after fa-. The print marks the doubled bāʾ of yuḥibbunī.

sentences.t: فَقَدَّمَتْ لَهُ الْأُمَرَاءُ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ بِقَدْرِ هِمَّتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qaddamat lahu al-umarāʾu kullu wāḥidin bi-qadri himmatihi
sentences.l: And the emirs presented to him, each one according to the measure of his ambition.
sentences.i: So the emirs brought him presents, each as generously as his spirit allowed.
sentences.n: qaddamat, feminine singular with a plural of persons before it: common with broken plurals. himma, “aspiration, zeal”, here “generosity of spirit”.

sentences.t: وَسَمَّاهُ السُّلْطَانُ الزَّبَلْكَانَ وَلَقَّبَهُ بِالْمُجَاهِدِ
sentences.tr: wa-sammāhu al-sulṭānu al-zabalkāna wa-laqqabahu bi-al-mujāhidi
sentences.l: And the sultan named him al-Zabalkān and surnamed him al-Mujāhid.
sentences.i: The sultan gave him the name al-Zabalkān, and the title al-Mujāhid, “the Warrior for the Faith”.
sentences.n: al-Zabalkān is built on zibl, “dung”: “the dung-man”, a joke on the wish he made. al-Mujāhid, “the one who strives (in holy war)”, is a regnal title of the kind real sultans bore. laqqaba bi-, “to give a title”: bi- introduces the title. The print marks the doubled qāf of laqqabahu.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا تَكَامَلَتْ حَوَائِجُهُ خَرَجَ وَصُحْبَتَهُ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَطَلَعَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ لِيُوَدِّعَهُ وَيَطْلُبَ مِنْهُ إِذْنًا بِالسَّفَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā takāmalat ḥawāʾijuhu kharaja wa-ṣuḥbatahu al-wazīru dandānu wa-ṭalaʿa ilā al-maliki li-yuwaddiʿahu wa-yaṭluba minhu idhnan bi-al-safari
sentences.l: And when his needs were complete, he went out, and in his company the vizier Dandān, and went up to the king to bid him farewell and ask of him leave for the journey.
sentences.i: When everything he needed was ready, he set out with the vizier Dandān in his company, and went up to the king to take his leave and ask permission to depart.
sentences.n: ṣuḥbatahu, “in his company”, an accusative of accompaniment much used in this text. ṭalaʿa, “to go up”, to the citadel. The print marks the doubled dāl of yuwaddiʿahu.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ وَعَانَقَةُ وَأَوْصَاهُ بِالْعَدْلِ بَيْنَ الرَّعِيَّةِ ثُمَّ أَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ الْأُهْبَةَ لِلْجِهَادِ بَعْدَ سَنَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma lahu al-maliku wa-ʿānaqahu wa-awṣāhu bi-al-ʿadli bayna al-raʿiyyati thumma amarahu an yaʾkhudha al-uhbata li-al-jihādi baʿda sanatayni
sentences.l: And the king rose for him and embraced him and charged him with justice among the subjects; then he commanded him to take the preparation for the holy war after two years.
sentences.i: The king rose for him and embraced him, and charged him to deal justly among his subjects; then he ordered him to make ready for the holy war two years from then.
sentences.n: The print writes ʿānaqahu with ة for the pronoun ه (وعانقة). awṣā bi-, “to enjoin (something)”. raʿiyya, “the flock”, the ruler's subjects. uhba, “readiness, equipment”.

sentences.t: وَوَدَّعَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا وَسَارَ الْمَلِكُ الْمُجَاهِدُ الْمُسَمَّى بِالزَّبَلْكَانِ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَوْصَاهُ الْمَلِكُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ بِالرَّعِيَّةِ خَيْرًا
sentences.tr: wa-waddaʿa baʿḍuhum baʿḍan wa-sāra al-maliku al-mujāhidu al-musammā bi-al-zabalkāni baʿda an awṣāhu al-maliku ḍawʾu al-makāni bi-al-raʿiyyati khayran
sentences.l: And they bade farewell some of them to others, and King al-Mujāhid, the one named al-Zabalkān, set out, after King Ḍawʾ al-Makān had charged him with the subjects well.
sentences.i: They bade each other farewell, and King al-Mujāhid, called al-Zabalkān, set out, once King Ḍawʾ al-Makān had charged him to treat his subjects well.
sentences.n: awṣāhu bi-al-raʿiyyati khayran, “charged him with the subjects (for) good”: told him to be good to them. The print marks the doubled dāl of waddaʿa and the doubled mīm of al-musammā.

sentences.t: وَقَدَّمَتْ لَهُ الْأُمَرَاءُ الْمَمَالِيكَ وَالْخَدَمَ فَبَلَغُوا خَمْسَةَ آلَافِ مَمْلُوكٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qaddamat lahu al-umarāʾu al-mamālīka wa-al-khadama fa-balaghū khamsata ālāfi mamlūkin
sentences.l: And the emirs presented to him the mamluks and the servants, and they reached five thousand mamluks.
sentences.i: The emirs gave him mamluks and servants, until they came to five thousand mamluks.
sentences.n: mamlūk, “owned”: a slave-soldier, bought and trained for war. The print writes ālāf with its madda (آلاف).

sentences.t: وَرَكِبُوا خَلْفَهُ وَرَكِبَ الْحَاجِبُ الْكَبِيرُ وَمُقَدَّمُ الدَّيْلَمِ بَهْرَامُ وَمُقَدَّمُ الْعَجَمِ رُسْتَمُ وَمُقَدَّمُ الْعَرَبِ تُرْكَاشُ وَهُمْ فِي خِدْمَتِهِ وَتَوْدِيعِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-rakibū khalfahu wa-rakiba al-ḥājibu al-kabīru wa-muqaddamu al-daylami bahrāmu wa-muqaddamu al-ʿajami rustamu wa-muqaddamu al-ʿarabi turkāshu wa-hum fī khidmatihi wa-tawdīʿihi
sentences.l: And they rode behind him; and the Great Chamberlain rode, and the chief of the Daylam, Bahrām, and the chief of the Persians, Rustam, and the chief of the Arabs, Turkāsh, they being in his service and his farewell.
sentences.i: They rode behind him; and with them rode the Great Chamberlain, Bahrām the chief of the Daylam, Rustam the chief of the Persians and Turkāsh the chief of the Arabs, attending him and seeing him on his way.
sentences.n: muqaddam, “one put in front”: a commander. The Daylam are the hill-people south of the Caspian; al-ʿajam are the Persians, and non-Arabs generally.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالُوا سَائِرِينَ مَعَهُ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ عَادُوا إِلَى بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zālū sāʾirīna maʿahu thalāthata ayyāmin thumma ʿādū ilā baghdāda
sentences.l: And they did not cease journeying with him three days; then they returned to Baghdad.
sentences.i: They rode on with him for three days, and then went back to Baghdad.
sentences.n: The print spells thalātha without its long alif (ثلثة); the small alif shows it.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلِ السُّلْطَانُ الزَّبَلْكَانُ وَالْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُمْ مِنَ الْعَسَاكِرِ سَائِرِينَ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazali al-sulṭānu al-zabalkānu wa-al-wazīru dandānu wa-man maʿahum mina al-ʿasākiri sāʾirīna ilā an waṣalū ilā dimashqa
sentences.l: And the sultan al-Zabalkān and the vizier Dandān and whoever (was) with them of the troops did not cease journeying, until they arrived at Damascus.
sentences.i: Sultan al-Zabalkān, the vizier Dandān and the troops with them journeyed on until they reached Damascus.
sentences.n: lam yazal … sāʾirīna, “did not cease journeying”: lam yazal, like kāna, takes its complement in the accusative. ilā an, “until”, here with a past verb.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتِ الْأَخْبَارُ قَدْ وَصَلَتْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلَى أَجْنِحَةِ الطُّيُورِ بِأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ سَلْطَنَ عَلَى دِمَشْقَ سُلْطَانًا يُقَالُ لَهُ الزَّبَلْكَانُ وَلَقَّبَهُ بِالْمُجَاهِدِ
sentences.tr: wa-kānati al-akhbāru qad waṣalat ilayhim ʿalā ajniḥati al-ṭuyūri bi-anna al-malika ḍawʾa al-makāni salṭana ʿalā dimashqa sulṭānan yuqālu lahu al-zabalkānu wa-laqqabahu bi-al-mujāhidi
sentences.l: And the tidings had arrived to them on the wings of the birds, that King Ḍawʾ al-Makān had sultaned over Damascus a sultan who is called al-Zabalkān, and had surnamed him with al-Mujāhid.
sentences.i: News had already reached the people there by carrier pigeon that King Ḍawʾ al-Makān had set over Damascus a sultan named al-Zabalkān, and had given him the title al-Mujāhid.
sentences.n: ilayhim, “to them”: to the people of Damascus, who are not named. ʿalā ajniḥat al-ṭuyūr, “on the wings of the birds”: by carrier pigeon, the fast post of the time. salṭana, “to make someone sultan”, a verb made from sulṭān; salṭana ʿalā, “to make sultan over”. laqqabahu bi-al-mujāhid, as above.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ زُيِّنَتْ لَهُ الْمَدِينَةُ وَخَرَجَ كُلُّ مَنْ فِي دِمَشْقَ لِلْفُرْجَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣala ilā dimashqa zuyyinat lahu al-madīnatu wa-kharaja kullu man fī dimashqa li-al-furjati
sentences.l: And when he arrived at Damascus, the city was adorned for him, and everyone who (was) in Damascus went out for the spectacle.
sentences.i: When he reached Damascus the city was decked out for him, and the whole of Damascus came out to watch.
sentences.n: furja, “a sight, a show”, a word of the spoken language (in Classical Arabic furja is “relief”); li-al-furja, “to see the sight”. The print marks the doubled yāʾ of zuyyinat.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ السُّلْطَانُ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ فِي مَوْكِبٍ عَظِيمٍ وَطَلَعَ الْقَلْعَةَ وَجَلَسَ عَلَى سَرِيرِ الْمَمْلَكَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala al-sulṭānu ilā dimashqa fī mawkibin ʿaẓīmin wa-ṭalaʿa al-qalʿata wa-jalasa ʿalā sarīri al-mamlakati
sentences.l: And the sultan entered into Damascus in a great procession, and went up the citadel, and sat upon the throne of the kingdom.
sentences.i: The sultan made his entry into Damascus in a great procession, went up to the citadel and sat on the throne of the realm.
sentences.n: ṭalaʿa al-qalʿata, “went up the citadel”, with the place as a direct object, the spoken usage. sarīr, “couch, throne”.

sentences.t: وَوَقَفَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ فِي خِدْمَتِهِ يُعَرِّفُهُ مَنَازِلَ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَمَرَاتِبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِ وَيُقَبِّلُونَ يَدَيْهِ وَيَدْعُونَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-waqafa al-wazīru dandānu fī khidmatihi yuʿarrifuhu manāzila al-umarāʾi wa-marātibahum wa-hum yadkhulūna ʿalayhi wa-yuqabbilūna yadayhi wa-yadʿūna lahu
sentences.l: And the vizier Dandān stood in his service, making-him-know the stations of the emirs and their ranks, while they were entering upon him and kissing his two hands and praying for him.
sentences.i: The vizier Dandān stood in attendance on him, telling him the standing and rank of each of the emirs as they came in to him, kissed his hands and called down blessings on him.
sentences.n: yuʿarrifuhu, “acquainting him with”: the new ruler, a stoker until lately, has to learn who ranks where. daʿā lahu, “to pray for someone”. The print marks the doubled letters of yuʿarrifuhu and yuqabbilūna.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَلِكُ الزَّبَلْكَانُ وَخَلَعَ وَأَعْطَى وَوَهَبَ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbala ʿalayhimu al-maliku al-zabalkānu wa-khalaʿa wa-aʿṭā wa-wahaba
sentences.l: And King al-Zabalkān turned-toward them, and robed and gave and bestowed.
sentences.i: King al-Zabalkān received them graciously, and gave out robes of honour, gifts and presents.
sentences.n: aqbala ʿalā, “to turn to someone with favour”. khalaʿa, “to take off”, used with no object for bestowing robes of honour (khilaʿ), the garment a ruler takes off and gives away.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ فَتَحَ خَزَائِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ وَأَنْفَقَهَا عَلَى جَمِيعِ الْعَسَاكِرِ كَبِيرًا وَصَغِيرًا وَحَكَمَ وَعَدَلَ
sentences.tr: thumma fataḥa khazāʾina al-amwāli wa-anfaqahā ʿalā jamīʿi al-ʿasākiri kabīran wa-ṣaghīran wa-ḥakama wa-ʿadala
sentences.l: Then he opened the treasuries of the moneys and spent them upon all the troops, great and small, and he ruled and was-just.
sentences.i: Then he opened the treasuries and spent their wealth on all the troops, great and small, and he governed and dealt justly.
sentences.n: kabīran wa-ṣaghīran, “great and small”, in the accusative as a set phrase: “high and low alike”.

sentences.t: وَشَرَعَ الزَّبَلْكَانُ فِي تَجْهِيزِ بِنْتِ السُّلْطَانِ شَرْكَانَ السِّتِّ قَضَى فَكَانَ وَجَعَلَ لَهَا مِحَفَّةً مِنَ الْإِبْرِيسَمِ
sentences.tr: wa-sharaʿa al-zabalkānu fī tajhīzi binti al-sulṭāni sharrukāna al-sitti qaḍā fakāna wa-jaʿala lahā miḥaffatan mina al-ibrīsami
sentences.l: And al-Zabalkān set about the equipping of the daughter of the sultan Sharrukān, the Lady Qaḍā Fakān, and made for her a litter of the silk.
sentences.i: And al-Zabalkān set about making ready the daughter of Sultan Sharrukān, the Lady Qaḍā Fakān, for her journey, and had a litter of silk made for her.
sentences.n: tajhīz, “equipping, fitting out” for the journey. miḥaffa, “a litter”, a covered seat carried by camels or mules for women travellers. ibrīsam, “raw silk”, a Persian word. al-sitt, “the lady”, as with the Lady Dunyā.

sentences.t: وَجَهَّزَ الْوَزِيرَ وَقَدَّمَ لَهُ شَيْأً مِنَ الْمَالِ فَأَبَى الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَنْتَ قَرِيبُ عَهْدٍ بِالْمُلْكِ وَرُبَّمَا تَحْتَاجُ إِلَى الْأَمْوَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-jahhaza al-wazīra wa-qaddama lahu shayʾan mina al-māli fa-abā al-wazīru dandānu wa-qāla lahu anta qarību ʿahdin bi-al-mulki wa-rubbamā taḥtāju ilā al-amwāli
sentences.l: And he equipped the vizier, and offered him something of the money; but the vizier Dandān refused, and said to him: You (are) near of acquaintance with the kingship, and perhaps you will need the moneys.
sentences.i: He fitted out the vizier as well and offered him a sum of money, but the vizier Dandān refused it, saying, “You are new to the throne, and you may well need the money yourself.
sentences.n: shayʾan is printed شيأً, with the hamza on an alif and the tanwīn marked, a common spelling in this edition. qarīb ʿahd bi-, “lately come to”: literally “near of acquaintance with”, bi- marking what one has newly met. rubbamā, “perhaps”.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ هٰذَا نَقْبَلُ مِنْكَ وَنُرْسِلُ إِلَيْكَ نَطْلُبُ مَالًا لِلْجِهَادِ أَوْ غَيْرِ ذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda hādhā naqbalu minka wa-nursilu ilayka naṭlubu mālan li-al-jihādi aw ghayri dhālika
sentences.l: And after this we will accept from you, and we will send to you (and) seek money for the holy-war or other-than that.
sentences.i: Later on we will accept it from you, and send to you asking for money for the holy war, or for whatever else is needed.”
sentences.n: naṭlubu, “we seek”, follows nursilu with no link word, to say what the sending is for: Middle Arabic often strings verbs like this. aw ghayri dhālika, “or (for) something else”, in the genitive like al-jihād.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا تَهَيَّأَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ لِلسَّفَرِ رَكِبَ السُّلْطَانُ الْمُجَاهِدُ إِلَى وَدَاعِ الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ وَأَحْضَرَ قَضَى فَكَانَ وَأَرْكَبَهَا فِى الْمِحَفَّةِ وَأَرْسَلَ مَعَهَا عَشْرَ جَوَارٍ بِرَسْمِ الْخِدْمَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā tahayyaʾa al-wazīru dandānu li-al-safari rakiba al-sulṭānu al-mujāhidu ilā wadāʿi al-wazīri dandāna wa-aḥḍara qaḍā fakāna wa-arkabahā fī al-miḥaffati wa-arsala maʿahā ʿashra jawārin bi-rasmi al-khidmati
sentences.l: And when the vizier Dandān had made-ready for the journey, the sultan al-Mujāhid rode to the farewell of the vizier Dandān; and he had Qaḍā Fakān brought, and mounted her in the litter, and sent with her ten slave-girls by way of the service.
sentences.i: When the vizier Dandān was ready to set out, Sultan al-Mujāhid rode out to see him off. He had Qaḍā Fakān brought, set her in the litter, and sent ten slave-girls with her to wait on her.
sentences.n: The print marks the doubled yāʾ of tahayyaʾa and writes its hamza on an alif (تهيّأ). jawārin, plural of jāriya, “slave-girl”. bi-rasm al-khidma, “by order of service”: bi-rasm, “assigned to, for the purpose of”, is a phrase of the chancery.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَأَنْ سَافَرَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ رَجَعَ الْمَلِكُ الْمُجَاهِدُ إِلَى مَمْلَكَتِهِ لِيُدَبِّرَهَا وَاهْتَمَّ بِآلَةِ السِّلَاحِ وَصَارَ يَنْتَظِرُ الْوَقْتَ الَّذِي يُرْسِلُ إِلَيْهِ فِيهِ الْمَلِكُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda an sāfara al-wazīru dandānu rajaʿa al-maliku al-mujāhidu ilā mamlakatihi li-yudabbirahā wa-ihtamma bi-ālati al-silāḥi wa-ṣāra yantaẓiru al-waqta alladhī yursilu ilayhi fīhi al-maliku ḍawʾu al-makāni
sentences.l: And after the vizier Dandān had travelled, King al-Mujāhid returned to his kingdom to manage it, and busied-himself with the gear of the weapons, and took-to awaiting the time in which King Ḍawʾ al-Makān would send to him.
sentences.i: After the vizier Dandān had gone, King al-Mujāhid went back to his kingdom to govern it. He busied himself with arms and the gear of war, and waited for the time when King Ḍawʾ al-Makān would send for him.
sentences.n: The print has اوزبر, a misprint for الوزير, corrected here. The print runs baʿda an together (وبعدان), and marks the doubled letters of yudabbirahā and ihtamma. ihtamma bi-, “to take care of, busy oneself with”. ālat al-silāḥ, “the gear of arms”, war equipment. He is waiting for the call to the holy war, which the king had set two years off.

sentences.t: هٰذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ السُّلْطَانِ الزَّبَلْكَانِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri al-sulṭāni al-zabalkāni
sentences.l: This (is) what was of the affair of the sultan al-Zabalkān.
sentences.i: So much for Sultan al-Zabalkān.
sentences.n: The storyteller's formula for closing one thread, answered by wa-ammā mā kāna min amri … in the next sentence.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يَزَلْ يَقْطَعُ الْمَرَاحِلَ بِقَضَى فَكَانَ وَسَارَ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى الرَّحْبَةِ بَعْدَ شَهْرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-wazīri dandāna fa-innahu lam yazal yaqṭaʿu al-marāḥila bi-qaḍā fakāna wa-sāra ḥattā waṣala ilā al-raḥbati baʿda shahrin
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of the vizier Dandān, he did not cease cutting the stages with Qaḍā Fakān, and journeyed until he arrived at al-Raḥba after a month.
sentences.i: As for the vizier Dandān, he travelled on, stage after stage, with Qaḍā Fakān, until after a month he reached al-Raḥba;
sentences.n: The print has اوزبر, a misprint for الوزير, and اى, a misprint for الى; both are corrected here. The print runs mā kāna together (ماكان). qaṭaʿa al-marāḥil, “to cut the stages”: to cover the day's marches one after another; bi- here is “with”, marking whom he takes along. al-Raḥba is the town on the Euphrates on the road from Syria to Iraq; the print itself marks the fatḥa on its rāʾ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَارَ حَتَّى أَشْرَفَ عَلَى بَغْدَادَ وَأَرْسَلَ أَعْلَمَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ بِقُدُومِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma sāra ḥattā ashrafa ʿalā baghdāda wa-arsala aʿlama ḍawʾa al-makāni bi-qudūmihi
sentences.l: Then he journeyed until he looked-down upon Baghdad, and sent (and) informed Ḍawʾ al-Makān of his arrival.
sentences.i: then he went on until Baghdad lay before him, and sent word to Ḍawʾ al-Makān that he had come.
sentences.n: ashrafa ʿalā, “to come within sight of”. arsala aʿlama, “he sent, he informed”: two verbs side by side with no link, for “he sent to inform”; the messenger, the object of arsala, goes unsaid. aʿlama X bi-, “to inform X of”: bi- marks the news.

sentences.t: فَرَكِبَ وَخَرَجَ إِلَى لِقَائِهِ فَأَرَادَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ أَنْ يَتَرَجَّلَ فَأَقْسَمَ عَلَيْهِ الْمَلِكُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ أَنْ لَا يَفْعَلَ
sentences.tr: fa-rakiba wa-kharaja ilā liqāʾihi fa-arāda al-wazīru dandānu an yatarajjala fa-aqsama ʿalayhi al-maliku ḍawʾu al-makāni an lā yafʿala
sentences.l: And he rode and went out to his meeting; and the vizier Dandān wanted to dismount, but King Ḍawʾ al-Makān adjured him that he not do (it).
sentences.i: The king mounted and rode out to meet him. The vizier Dandān made to dismount, but King Ḍawʾ al-Makān begged him on his oath not to.
sentences.n: tarajjala, “to get down from one's mount and go on foot”, here as a mark of respect for the king; the print marks its doubled jīm. aqsama ʿalayhi an, “he adjured him to”.

sentences.t: فَسَاقَ جَوَادَهُ حَتَّى جَاءَ إِلَى جَانِبِهِ وَسَأَلَهُ عَنِ الزَّبَلْكَانِ الْمُجَاهِدِ
sentences.tr: fa-sāqa jawādahu ḥattā jāʾa ilā jānibihi wa-saʾalahu ʿani al-zabalkāni al-mujāhidi
sentences.l: And he drove his steed until he came to his side, and asked him about al-Zabalkān al-Mujāhid.
sentences.i: He urged his horse on until he was riding beside him, and asked him about al-Zabalkān al-Mujāhid.
sentences.n: sāqa, “to drive, urge on”; jawād, “a fine horse, a steed”. The Arabic does not say who rides up to whom; most likely the king brings his horse alongside the vizier's.

sentences.t: فَأَعْلَمَهُ أَنَّهُ بِخَيْرٍ وَأَعْلَمَهُ بِقُدُومِ قَضَى فَكَانَ بِنْتِ أَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿlamahu annahu bi-khayrin wa-aʿlamahu bi-qudūmi qaḍā fakāna binti akhīhi sharrukāna
sentences.l: And he informed him that he (was) in good (state), and informed him of the arrival of Qaḍā Fakān, the daughter of his brother Sharrukān.
sentences.i: The vizier told him that al-Zabalkān was well, and told him too that Qaḍā Fakān, his brother Sharrukān's daughter, had come.
sentences.n: bi-khayr, “in good state, well”: bi- of the condition one is in.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ وَقَالَ لَهُ دُونَكَ وَالرَّاحَةَ مِنْ تَعَبِ السَّفَرِ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ تَعَالَ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa wa-qāla lahu dūnaka wa-al-rāḥata min taʿabi al-safari thalāthata ayyāmin thumma baʿda dhālika taʿāla ʿindī
sentences.l: And he rejoiced, and said to him: Before-you, and the rest from the toil of the journey, three days; then after that come to me.
sentences.i: He was glad, and said to him, “Go now and rest from the hardships of the road for three days; after that, come to me.”
sentences.n: dūnaka, “before you”, is the old word of urging, “there it is, take it”, with what is urged in the accusative; the wa- before al-rāḥa is odd, and the phrase reads as “off with you, and to your rest”. thalātha is printed without its long alif and with the small alif (ثلٰثة). taʿāla ʿindī, “come to me”, literally “come at my place”, the spoken usage.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ حُبًّا وَكَرَامَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḥubban wa-karāmatan
sentences.l: And he said: (With) love and honour.
sentences.i: He answered, “Gladly, and with honour.”
sentences.n: ḥubban wa-karāmatan, “out of love and honour”, the courteous formula for agreeing to a request.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ وَطَلَعَ الْمَلِكُ إِلَى قَصْرِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra tawajjaha ilā manzilihi wa-ṭalaʿa al-maliku ilā qaṣrihi
sentences.l: Then the vizier betook-himself to his dwelling, and the king went up to his palace.
sentences.i: Then the vizier went off to his own house, and the king went up to his palace.
sentences.n: The print marks the doubled jīm of tawajjaha.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ عَلَى ابْنَةِ أَخِيهِ قَضَى فَكَانَ وَهِيَ ابْنَةُ ثَمَانِ سِنِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala ʿalā ibnati akhīhi qaḍā fakāna wa-hiya ibnatu thamāni sinīna
sentences.l: And he entered upon the daughter of his brother, Qaḍā Fakān, and she (was) a daughter of eight years.
sentences.i: He went in to his niece Qaḍā Fakān, who was then eight years old.
sentences.n: ibnat thamān sinīn, “daughter of eight years”, the usual way of giving a girl's age. The print marks the kasra of hiya (وهِي).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا فَرِحَ بِهَا وَحَزِنَ عَلَى أَبِيهَا وَفَصَّلَ لَهَا ثِيَابًا وَأَعْطَى لَهَا مَصَاغًا وَحُلِيًّا عَظِيمًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā fariḥa bihā wa-ḥazina ʿalā abīhā wa-faṣṣala lahā thiyāban wa-aʿṭā lahā maṣāghan wa-ḥuliyyan ʿaẓīman
sentences.l: And when he saw her, he rejoiced in her and grieved over her father; and he cut-out for her clothes, and gave to her wrought-gold and ornaments, great.
sentences.i: When he saw her he was glad of her, and grieved for her father. He had clothes cut out and made for her, and gave her a great store of gold work and jewels.
sentences.n: faṣṣala, “to cut out (cloth for a garment)”; the print marks its doubled ṣād. aʿṭā lahā, “gave to her”, with li- where Classical aʿṭā takes two direct objects, a spoken habit. maṣāgh, “wrought gold and silver, jewellery”; ḥuliyy, plural of ḥaly, “ornaments”. The print writes raʾāhā with its madda (رآها).

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَأَنْ يُبَيِّتُوهَا مَعَ ابْنِهِ كَانَ مَا كَانَ فِي مَكَانٍ وَاحِدٍ
sentences.tr: wa-amara an yubayyitūhā maʿa ibnihi kāna mā kāna fī makānin wāḥidin
sentences.l: And he commanded that they make-her-spend-the-night with his son Kān Mā Kān in one place.
sentences.i: And he gave orders that she should sleep in the same room as his son Kān Mā Kān.
sentences.n: The print runs amara an together (وامران), and marks the doubled yāʾ of yubayyitūhā, “that they lodge her for the night”, from bāta, “to spend the night”. The two cousins are to be brought up together.

sentences.t: فَطَلَعَا أَذْكَى أَهْلِ زَمَانِهِمَا وَأَشْجَعَ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaʿā adhkā ahli zamānihimā wa-ashjaʿa
sentences.l: And the two came-out the cleverest of the people of their time, and the bravest.
sentences.i: The two of them grew up the cleverest and the bravest of all the people of their day.
sentences.n: ṭalaʿa, “to come up”: in the spoken language “to turn out, grow up to be”, with its complement in the accusative, as after kāna. ashjaʿa, “bravest”, has no complement of its own; ahli zamānihimā is understood again.

sentences.t: غَيْرَ أَنَّ قَضَى فَكَانَ طَلَعَتْ صَاحِبَةَ تَدْبِيرٍ وَعَقْلٍ وَخِبْرَةٍ بِعَوَاقِبِ الْأُمُورِ وَطَلَعَ كَانَ مَاكَانَ سَمْحًا كَرِيمًا لَا يُفَكِّرُ فِي عَاقِبَةِ شَيْءٍ
sentences.tr: ghayra anna qaḍā fakāna ṭalaʿat ṣāḥibata tadbīrin wa-ʿaqlin wa-khibratin bi-ʿawāqibi al-umūri wa-ṭalaʿa kāna mā kāna samḥan karīman lā yufakkiru fī ʿāqibati shayʾin
sentences.l: Except that Qaḍā Fakān came-out a mistress of management and reason and knowledge of the outcomes of the affairs, and Kān Mā Kān came-out open-handed, generous, not thinking about the outcome of anything.
sentences.i: But Qaḍā Fakān grew up prudent and sensible, with a shrewd eye for where things would lead, while Kān Mā Kān grew up open-handed and generous, never stopping to think where anything would end.
sentences.n: ṣāḥibat tadbīr, “a mistress of management”: a woman of good judgement. khibra bi-, “knowledge of, experience in”. ʿawāqib, plural of ʿāqiba, “outcome, end”. The print runs mā kāna together in Kān Mā Kān's name here (كان ماكان), and marks the doubled kāf of yufakkiru.

sentences.t: فَكَبِرَ الِاثْنَانِ وَصَارَ لَهُمَا مِنَ الْعُمْرِ عَشْرُ سِنِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-kabira al-ithnāni wa-ṣāra lahumā mina al-ʿumri ʿashru sinīna
sentences.l: And the two grew-big, and there came-to-be for them of the age ten years.
sentences.i: The two grew older, until they were ten years old.
sentences.n: ṣāra lahumā mina al-ʿumri, “there came to be to them, of age”: they reached the age of.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتْ قَضَيٰ فَكَانَ تَرْكَبُ الْخَيْلَ وَتَطْلُعُ مَعَ ابْنِ عَمِّهَا فِى الْبَرِّ وَتَسُوقُ بِهِ وَتُوَسِّعُ فِى الْبَرِّ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārat qaḍā fakāna tarkabu al-khayla wa-taṭluʿu maʿa ibni ʿammihā fī al-barri wa-tasūqu bihi wa-tuwassiʿu fī al-barri
sentences.l: And Qaḍā Fakān took-to riding the horses, and going-out with the son of her paternal-uncle into the open-land, and driving with him, and going-wide in the open-land.
